parts.label: (a)
hints: Hint 1: Think of AM as combining two waves - a high-frequency carrier that can travel far, and a low-frequency audio signal that carries the sound. Which one actually travels to the receiver?
Hint 2: Focus on the word amplitude. Which wave provides the amplitude that changes, and which wave controls how it changes in time?
parts.proper_answer: The amplitude of the carrier wave is made to vary in synchrony with the displacement of the information (audio) signal.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Picture the two waves**
Think of a tall, fast oscillation - this is the carrier wave at radio frequency, e.g. hundreds of kHz. It has constant frequency but on its own it carries no sound. Then think of the slow audio signal, e.g. speech or music, whose displacement up and down represents the sound you want to send.

Step 2: **What modulation does**
In amplitude modulation the carrier keeps the same frequency, but its height - its amplitude - is no longer constant. At any instant, the envelope of the carrier copies the displacement of the audio signal. So a loud positive audio displacement makes a large carrier amplitude, and so on. That is why it is called amplitude modulation.

parts.label: (b)(i)
hints: Hint 1: Look at Fig. 5.1 and pick out the tall central line - that is the carrier. Note its frequency in kHz and remember what speed all radio waves travel at in free space.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify the carrier frequency**
The large amplitude line in the centre of Fig. 5.1 is the carrier. It is at $f = 300\text{ kHz} = 300 \times 10^3\text{ Hz}$. The smaller spread on either side are the sidebands created by modulation.

Step 2: **Use the wave equation**
All electromagnetic waves travel at $c = 3.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Use: $$c = f \lambda$$ $$\lambda = \frac{c}{f} = \frac{3.0 \times 10^8}{300 \times 10^3} = 1000\text{ m}$$

parts.label: (b)(ii)
hints: Hint 1: Bandwidth means the total spread of frequencies occupied by the whole modulated signal. Look at the lowest and highest frequencies where the signal in Fig. 5.1 starts and ends.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Read the limits from the spectrum**
The modulated wave extends from a minimum frequency $f_{min} = 292\text{ kHz}$ to a maximum frequency $f_{max} = 308\text{ kHz}$ in Fig. 5.1.

Step 2: **Subtract to get the width**
Bandwidth is the range: $$\text{bandwidth} = f_{max} - f_{min} = 308 - 292 = 16\text{ kHz}$$

parts.label: (b)(iii)
hints: Hint 1: Remember the modulated signal has two mirror-image sidebands, one above and one below the carrier. How is the total bandwidth related to the highest audio frequency?
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Link sidebands to audio**
An audio frequency $f_a$ produces one component at $f_c + f_a$ and one at $f_c - f_a$, where $f_c$ is the carrier. So the total spread is twice the audio frequency.

Step 2: **Halve the bandwidth**
$$f_{audio,max} = \frac{\text{bandwidth}}{2} = \frac{16\text{ kHz}}{2} = 8.0\text{ kHz}$$ This is the difference between the carrier at $300\text{ kHz}$ and the edge at $308\text{ kHz}$.

parts.label: (c)
hints: Hint 1: Start by recalling how attenuation in decibels is defined from the ratio of transmitted power to received power.
Hint 2: Substitute the given expression for $P_R$ in terms of $P_T$ and $x$ into that dB expression, so $P_T$ cancels and only $x$ remains.
Hint 3: You will have an equation of the form $73 = 10\lg(...x...)$. Undo the log by dividing by 10 then using powers of 10 to solve for $x$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Write attenuation with logs**
Attenuation measures how much power is lost, in decibels: $$\text{attenuation} = 10\lg\left(\frac{P_T}{P_R}\right)$$ Here it is $73\text{ dB}$, so: $$73 = 10\lg\left(\frac{P_T}{P_R}\right)$$

Step 2: **Insert the given power law**
You are told: $$P_R = \frac{0.082 P_T}{x^2}$$ So the ratio is: $$\frac{P_T}{P_R} = \frac{P_T}{0.082 P_T / x^2} = \frac{x^2}{0.082}$$ Hence: $$73 = 10\lg\left(\frac{x^2}{0.082}\right)$$ The unknown $P_T$ has cancelled nicely, as it should.

Step 3: **Solve for x**
Divide by 10: $$7.3 = \lg\left(\frac{x^2}{0.082}\right)$$ Undo $\lg$ with $10^{...}$: $$\frac{x^2}{0.082} = 10^{7.3}$$ $$x^2 = 0.082 \times 10^{7.3}$$ $$x = \sqrt{0.082 \times 10^{7.3}} \approx 1.3 \times 10^3\text{ m}$$ So $x \approx 1300\text{ m}$.
